utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Defence ready to continue the cross-examination of the expert witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Pilipovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, good morning.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Friday we stopped discussing documents 203, 1863, 1864, and 1865. These are the documents I showed you when we were speaking -- when we spoke about the truce and the measures that General Galic took.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could these four documents please be shown: 203, 1863, 1864, and 1865.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I think that on Friday you spoke about document 203, 22 November 1992, and you explained what General Galic did, what measures he took when he was appointed as corps commander.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned an entire series of measures taken by General Galic in order to support the truce. In front of me I have document 203 from the command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. The date is the 22nd of November, 1992. It's a protest to UNPROFOR. General Galic - at the time he was a colonel in the Sarajevo Romanija Corps - he requested that the truce be supported and that UNPROFOR take action with regard to the units of the 1st Corps of the BH army and he requested that this truce be maintained, because he said if the action wasn't interrupted, halted, the corps forces would be forced to take measures to respond to the situation, and "that would bring into question all the efforts to find a peaceful solution to the problems in Sarajevo and beyond."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the document the witness is talking about be put on the ELMO because the Bench has some problems in identifying the right -- and could the ELMO be zoomed in also on the upper part.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, did you read from item 1: "if those actions don't stop, the corps will be forced to respond adequately to the situation. It would put in question all the efforts for a peaceful solution to the problem in Sarajevo and beyond, and this is something that UNPROFOR is supporting too."

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I read that out. I wanted to emphasise the fact that you can see how at the beginning of his mandate General Galic insisted on maintaining the truce because that was an opportunity for peace. Otherwise, if it was necessary to respond to the provocations, the opening of fire on the part of the other side, violence would escalate, peace would be threatened, and then the chances of having a peaceful solution to the situation in Sarajevo would be reduced. So I concluded that he was in favour of a peaceful solution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, document 1863, 15 February 1993; 1865, 19th of June, 1993; and the document dated the 15th of February, do they also indicate the measures taken by General Stanislav Galic in order to cooperate with UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... With the unnumbered -- at least partly unnumbered series. Could whatever document is dealt with be put on the ELMO so that we can identify it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it was -- the Defence's intention, but since you had the documents, or rather, the registry, we were not in a position to make corrections, but corrections have been made in the registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not blaming you for anything, but we have one well-numbered set by now, which is in the hands of the registry. So if they are put on the ELMO, we can follow what the testimony is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, is this document 1863 a document that is from the Sarajevo Romanija Corps about determining the coordinates for UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The corps commander tells his subordinates, orders his subordinates to introduce the UNPROFOR coordinates in their working booklets so that they could be protected from possible action from the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, taken by the units of the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, could we have the document 1864.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a document dated the 15th of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the date is the 15th of February, 1993. It's an order in which General Galic ordered his subordinates to introduce the coordinates of observation points in the territory under the control of the BH army 1st Corps, and he forbids that within a radius of under 1.000 metres they should not take action in that area, and in this way he wanted to avoid any possible hit that might occur when the artillery is used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we have document 1865 too.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's also an order in which General Galic ordered his subordinates to cease hostilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, given the time that we have, that the Defence has now left, my colleague will continue with the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, General.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll start by showing you some documents. But to the extent that this is possible, could you please answer my questions by saying yes or no. This would be much appreciated because of our time restrictions. General, first of all, a document that we're going to show you, the number of the document is 278, 278. And at the same time, we are going to show you a map, with the assistance of the usher, and we will place it on the ELMO, as well as document number 278, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd appreciate it if we could show this to the general, document 278, in order not to waste too much time. Mr. President, these documents have been numbered. If we are going to lose some time, I'd appreciate it if this could be taken into account, if this could be added to the time that we have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you spoke about elevations around Sarajevo. Do you remember speaking about that or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, I don't think I heard you say anything about the Grdonj elevation. What was this elevation called? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Grdonj elevation? Well, I don't remember what the altitude was exactly, but I know where it is. I think it is about 805 metres. I think that that was the altitude.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What can you tell us, since we're talking about this now, what was the position, General -- I apologise, what was the army that held the positions on Grdonj; in other words, elevation 906? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units of the 1st Corps of the BH army held this position, elevation 906, and the positions that were just below, a little further to the east or to the south-east, that was in Sedrenik and the Sarajevo Romanija Corps held this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, very well. But on the elevation Grdonj itself, which army held the positions in the southern part of Grdonj?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the unit of the 1st Corps of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How do you know and who did you speak to about this in order to obtain this knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was partially able to see that from the maps that I had, from documents to an extent, and I was provided with the direct information from the command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, the 1st unit, General Lizdek.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, I would now like to examine document 278. You have it in front of you. It also has an ERN number 025 -- I apologise, 02056268. General, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a document that I had in front of me when I was writing my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it please be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we can recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a document that consists of a number of pages. Could you please give another document to the general so that he can go through it. Must I repeat that? Should I repeat that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You asked that another document -- another document. Which document did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked for a second document to be shown to the witness so that he could be able to go through it, thank you in advance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, having solved this problem, do you recognise this document? You said yes. What can you tell us about this document, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognised the document. It's an order from the commander of the 102nd Motorised Brigade from the 1st Corps of the BH army, and it's dated the 1st of February, 1994. In this document, he orders what the disposition of his subordinate units should be, battalions, divisions, companies, command posts, logistics, et cetera. And on the basis of that document, I drew a map. This order was represented with map symbols on the map, and you can see the positions in that part of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, I also asked for the map to be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you place this map, please, on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is as follows - and I'd like to say that the following number will be D235 - General, to the right of you, you have the map.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we speaking about this map?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. General, with regard to a second map that we are going to show you in a minute, for this area, the area to the north-west of Nedzarici, did you have a lot of information, more than the information you had for other companies or brigades? What can you tell us about the information you had, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In these areas, that is to say, positions in the town, from when the SRK was formed, the 3rd Motorised Brigade was based here, and then in the middle of 1993 it was renamed the 102nd Motorised Brigade. For this area of Sarajevo, I had the greatest amount of information, which is why I decided to represent the combat positions of those brigades in that part of the Sarajevo theatre of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, we're going to have to carry out an exercise very rapidly. And could you please answer these questions: There are some symbols on this map. Are these classical symbols that are usually used in the army?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could the technical booth please zoom in so that we could have a clear view of this map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you understood the question, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, could you zoom in.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drew this map on the basis of instructions for working maps, which were in force in the JNA, and which both sides in the conflict adopted. So according to those rules, how certain elements of the combat disposition and how certain elements of the unit should be represented, this is decided on. And in operative communications, one is very clear about what one can find there and what this means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. General, so that we can understand this matter, we'll start with the simplest things. Could you tell us what a triangle means with a flag. I can see a triangle and a flag attached to it with the number "2." What does it mean, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The triangle above which there is a flag with a "2", a number 2 in it, this is the map symbol for the command post of that battalion, that is, the 2nd Motorised Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, we also see other symbols such as a horizontal line, a half circle full, and two or three curves coming out of this circle, sort of.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean this symbol?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I don't want to guide you, but there is a full half circle under letters "BVG 2."

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see. You mean this. This is a map symbol for firing positions of the battalion firing group, and inside of this ellipse is a symbol for mortar, which means that this is the firing group of the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. General, under the word "Borbeni," please, to the far right, near the word -- under the "R" in the word "Borbeni," there is a sign depicting -- please look at the map. Under the letter "R" in the word "Borbeni" --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the AV booth zoom in on this so we can see clearly. That is, zoom in -- zoom out a little. Yes. Zoom out a little, please. That's it. Just a little further so that we can see the word "Borbeni," just a little more, some more, so that we see all of it. A little further out. Right. Please stop here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, under the word "Borbeni," under the letter "R," here is what I'm interested in. On the right side, to the right - the witness is pointing - this sign, these three lines, two of them shorter, the central one being longer, what does this depict? Yes, this sign.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a map symbol for firing positions of the brigade firing group, and these three circles depict, or rather, mean that this brigade firing group has three batteries. So these circles are map symbols for batteries, Howitzers, and mortars. So this firing group has two Howitzer batteries and one mortar -- or rather, two mortar batteries and one Howitzer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question is as follows: All the signs that we see on this map, with the exception of the flags, do all these signs depict positions where specific weaponry is located, or do they mean something else? I'm talking about the symbols on this map.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these symbols depicted on the map represent locations where armed men are located, even what you called triangles with little flags, those are command posts and command posts are protected, secured, by armed men, such as police units of the command posts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll pass to document 235.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So as not to waste time, could it be put in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the document. It is an order of the commander of the 1st Corps of the BH army for defence, dated 25th October 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please give me your comments, if any, on this document.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I would like us to look at this document where the commander of the 1st Corps sets out the areas of responsibility of his Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. subordinate brigades, and he orders that in these zones they organise combat positions. He explicitly sets out which unit or which brigade is in which area. On the second page of the document, under item 5, 5.1, that is, the commander orders to the commander of the 1st Motorised Brigade where and in which zone he should organise defence, in other words, where he should deploy his forces. He determines the positions and the command post for this brigade. This is a part of the town - and I'm sorry we don't have this central map with us to see which area this is - this is the north-west part of the town from Ugorsko to Visk [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're going to do the following: The map will be distributed with one copy put on the ELMO. I don't know if the usher can hear me. Thank you. One of these maps can be put on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me to finish my answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, right now -- yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So according to the same model of organisation of defence for the 102nd Brigade, which we saw on the ELMO with a lot of detail, the commander of the corps orders the 2nd, the 1st, the 5th, the 101st Brigade of the HVO, 15th, 105th, 4th, and all units of firing support and logistics to take up positions in the urban part of Sarajevo, with the exception of the 4th Brigade, which was occupying positions outside Hrasnica, that is, in the strict urban area. If you now imagine this city of Sarajevo, this strictly urban part, it was occupied by military forces in the identical manner as we saw on the map dealing with the 102nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to suggest with the Court's leave that our assistant, with the help of the usher, puts this open map behind you so that we can all see it. If not, it will have to be folded and put on the ELMO. Of course, if we have the Court's leave. Maybe the lady will be able to handle it on her own. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, we are now going to do this in this way so that we can see better. You see the map here?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make this map?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, do you have this pointer that you were using yesterday? Yes. Thank you. We see in the eastern part of this map a zone which is very representative, indicative, of military presence. Does it have anything in common with the little map that we saw a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very near that but further to the west we see another zone with military installations, that is, a zone right next to it, to the west, west to the zone, that is, between the two zones you indicated -- yes, this is it. And then to the north, there is a zone which apparently is devoid of military installations. Could you give us your comments: Why does it seem that in this zone there are less military targets or installations, and what can you tell us in general about this map?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am showing where one battalion of the Ilidza Brigade of the SRK was, and I didn't represent this as military targets because I was depicting military targets of the 1st Corps of the BH army in Sarajevo. In these areas I did not depict any targets because my idea was to show how they are positioned, how they are laid out in the urban part of the city, because my entire report focussed on the urban part of Sarajevo. But generally speaking, for the so-called peripheral non-urban areas, there is a separate document -- I don't know the exact number, but it passed through my hands. It was done in the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, and it identified about 370 targets. There is also a map of these targets where they are clearly depicted, and we can see that even this part is full of military resources of the 1st BH army Corps. However, I didn't represent them here. I was interested, rather, in the urban part. Here, in this urban part of Sarajevo not so many targets are depicted for the precise reason that in the documents that were available to me, I did not have as much information as for the areas where these targets are represented. In this part of Dobrinja, there was the 5th Brigade, the 101st Brigade. In this area there was the 6th Brigade. But for them I had less information, so I couldn't identify targets as I was able to in the localities where there are more of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record, perhaps, the areas that the witness has just pointed to should be indicated for the purposes of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please do so, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, gladly. But I have to say that he mentioned Dobrinja, whereas the witness clearly indicated clearly in the area of Dobrinja, that we know well. He said the 5th and the 105th. We have to see in the transcript. And he also mentioned the zone of Mojmilo, which --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was the 101st.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the 101st Motorised, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 6th, the 10th at Colina Kapa-Jewish cemetery, Kladovo and Cuprija the 1st, then Kozja Cuprija-Hladivode, Hladivode-Grdonj is the 3rd, the 7th was from Grdonj to Kobilja Glava, and thereon we enter the area of the 1st Brigade, which went up to Zabrdje, from then on there was the 2nd and the 102nd. I didn't depict the targets for these because this goes outside the urban part.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many brigades are on this map?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We don't see any brigades on this map. They were on the map of mutual deployment where we see 13 brigades but some of them are not visible because they did not have areas of responsibility. There were three forces for alternative assignments, such as the 1st Vikic Brigade, the special MUP Brigade, such as the Reconnaissance and Sabotage Brigade, such as the Independent Manoeuvring Battalion, that is, a number of battalions that did not have specified areas of responsibility in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two questions about this map, and we'll come back to it later: You mentioned a moment ago there was a brigade at Grdonj. Will you please check on this map. Where did you draw the line in Grdonj? And then with respect to elevation 906, do you assess this map is accurate in view of the information we obtained, oral and documentary?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I respond? We have the map in front of our eyes, all of us. We see that the northern border, near Grdonj, passes through a certain area. What I want to ask the witness is that he gives us his comment which concerns a line. It is not too much to ask in view of the time spent by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, in order to save time and not ask the witness to leave the courtroom, let me quickly state an objection on the grounds that the witness has testified that he created the map. It would, therefore, follow that he would think it was accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we heard a lot of evidence, especially on the situation of confrontation lines in the area you were just referring to by those who were present at that time. So therefore, this expert witness is not primarily a witness of fact, I would say. But if you think that he knows facts from his own observation, then this is Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. merely a matter of fact, it's not a matter of expertise where a line is. That's a fact. Could you please lay the basis for his knowledge. And if not, if there's no personal knowledge, then the Chamber will be able to compare this map with the evidence we've heard. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you took part in the peace negotiations in Geneva between the two parties in the capacity of expert. That's what you told us last time. At that time did you have in your possession military maps, detailed ones, that depicted the situation on the ground; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did have maps. I don't know whether they were detailed -- in fact, they were detailed, but I don't know if they were precise. I was just a participant in negotiations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But at that time did you know whether the Serb party - reply with yes or no - did you know whether this area of Grdonj was under Muslim control?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection. It's a leading question. And in light of the answers previously -- the witness's previous answer, there's a lack of foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're now asking whether a certain area was under the control of one party. Do I have to understand you that the expert witness should answer this question on the basis of the maps he just referred to, or is there any personal knowledge? It should be clear what the basis is for the facts on which this expert relies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About these two things, possibly the maps and possibly -- this is the purpose of my question. I'm asking him whether the representatives of the Serb side, in fact, the Serb side, indicated at these peace negotiations whether certain elevations were under Muslim control. And if yes, whether Grdonj was among them. I want to hear what he personally knows about it as a participant in the negotiations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you don't know, you just don't know.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, thank you. I would like us to go back to this map now. I would like us to see what was the maximum number of military installations, military targets, that we could find in Sarajevo or in theory if there were more of them than depicted, what could be the number from statistical information?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. It's a leading question. It calls for speculation, and it lacks probative value.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, gladly, Your Honour. I don't think it is a leading question. I was asking the witness whether he depicted everything he could. There are quasi-scientific ways of representing something without actually seeing. For instance, I can see a truck full of wheat and I don't necessarily have to wait. If I know the capacity and I can calculate and arithmetically determine how many tonnes of wheat there are in it. That's why I'm asking the witness by analogy. And I don't think it is speculation. We can calculate things in one or another way, for this clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if I do understand you well, you are asking the witness what, according to his experience, he would expect to be the number of and then I think you're asking about military installations, military targets. Your question is twofold. The first one is: What is the maximum number of military installations, military targets that we could find in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For instance -- first of all, if the total number is represented - yes or no; and second, if not, what can be said about it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I answer now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First let's try to get the question clear, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Do you know the total number of military installations that, as far as I understand, could be military targets in Sarajevo? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this urban part of Sarajevo, every day, according to my reckoning, there was over 1500 military installations that can be considered as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you. You said according to your reckoning. The first question is: Do you know it? And my second question -- my second question would be: Whether you could, on the basis of your experience, give a calculated guess as to the number? First, do you know it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please give us the answer. We don't have to guess then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Every day in the urban part of Sarajevo there was over 1500 targets. This can be calculated in a relatively reliable manner based on the structure of units and their deployment, which is depicted on the map of mutual deployment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand your answer to be that you have an opinion about it on the basis of your experience. Because if you calculate it, it's not that you know one, two, three, four, five. But if you say you have five units of such character, they would have -- they would need so and so much command posts or whatever. But -- so we do understand your answer to be a calculation on the basis of your experience. Please, then, explain to us how you calculate this. Or if you want to proceed -- I do understand that the outcome of your calculation was that there were over 1500.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the interval, perhaps we can put this map down. We don't want to spare -- to squander the manpower we have in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, while that's -- while that's being done, could I get the exhibit number for that map, please. It's not marked on my copy of the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On my copy, it's 1913 on the left top corner. Now -- yes, that's the -- this one is perfectly numbered, as far as my copy is concerned. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, could you please give us your answer about this calculation. Very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, under military doctrine, an average battery target, the target of a battery or a mortar company is deployed section in defence. It is very easy to calculate how many sections the 1st Corps had in the urban part of Sarajevo if you follow the areas of deployment of its brigades, by brigades and by battalions and companies, as I have shown on this other A4 map. If you do that, you know exactly the composition of company firing groups, battalion firing groups, brigade firing groups, company observation points, battalion command posts, the command posts of brigades, the logistics, including bases, quartermaster stations, technical stations, communication centres, radio devices, workshops, depots. And when you take all that into account and add it up, I calculated that there was 1.530 targets in Sarajevo every day. This is nothing too complicated. You don't have to be a rocket scientist to calculate this. You only need to know the structure of the troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you well, General, you are telling us that preceding from the hierarchy starting from brigade down, you know also that so much weaponry is needed for one brigade and so much manpower, and that's how you arrived at the figure of 1530. Is this your reasoning?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are the military resources that are determined by one battery target, by the target that a battery fires at. A battery can consist of four to six artillery pieces, mortars, cannons, or Howitzers. That's the target in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, another question about these targets: Let's take the number 1.500. Out of these 1.500 -- about these 1.500 targets, what can Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you tell us about the mobile nature of these targets? For example, were these targets embedded? Were they fixed, or the -- on the contrary, were they very mobile targets? Could you comment on this, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness just gave a list of 10 or 12 different types of targets. The question is not specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I do understand that the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you hear what I have to say, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just wanted to add one other element so that you could respond. I'm drawing your attention to the fact that the witness said that his number was based upon a calculation of certain types of targets, and I would like to ask you what your question was specifically about when you -- about types of targets or about specific factual targets. Because your question asked whether the targets were mobile and -- yes, please respond, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my question was vague, so that I should not be criticised for being leading. I'd appreciate it if this witness could tell us whether certain targets were mobile or fixed, and I did not want to be specific and say targets such as a machine-gun carried by a man, was this mobile or not? My question was vague, and I wanted the witness to answer on the basis of his experience and on the basis of his knowledge, on the basis of what he was able to see in the documents that he examined when compiling his report. Has the objection been rejected, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you may ask a question about this, but please make clear whether you are asking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'll move on to another subject, Mr. President, because I see that it is not possible to question the witness about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... I will ask a question. Could you tell us whether by nature of the targets you just mentioned, whether you could tell us whether they are by nature of a mobile character or of a fixed character.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The targets that I had mentioned -- among the targets that I had mentioned, there were some that were relatively fixed and there were others that were mobile, that could be moved. The structure of the army was such that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you now referring to targets of which you know the existence specifically, or are you talking about the targets by their very nature being mobile -- more or less mobile?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All these targets are mobile. But I'm talking about what I know about Sarajevo. You can see from the documents this is frequently the case, in relation to UNPROFOR observers and international military observers. Information was cited according to which officials from the 1st Corps of the BH army held their mortars and moved them from one place to another very easily, and this was very difficult for the Sarajevo Romanija Corps to neutralise, to deal with. So this part of the combat disposition was very mobile. They would fire a few mortars -- mortar shells from a certain position and then they would move, and this is how they'd provoke a response from the Army of Republika Srpska, or rather, from the units of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand that you specifically are pointing to the mobility of mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That of mortars and of the manoeuvring forces that provided the support force. In the 1st Brigade and in the 3rd Brigade these were the armoured battalions, the mixed artillery battalions and the self-propelled Howitzers which were in the Hum area and in the Velesic area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you have spoken about these weapons. With regard to the issue of mobility, what can you tell us about PAMs and similar weapons, PAMs, anti-aircraft machine-guns?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can move these weapons at any point in time. They are very mobile weapons in the battlefield.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the case in Sarajevo, according to the documents that you were able to examine; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same question for PATs, anti-aircraft cannons?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your answer?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, as a result, given that the number of tactical targets - the number of weapons was 1.500 according to your calculations - and the number of places where these targets were, could the number of positions be far greater given their mobile nature?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, I'll move on to a methodological question. The map that you had in front of you a minute ago was elaborated, and I think that you identified over 220 features. You marked over 220 features. Can you tell us how you proceeded, what methodology did you use to determine what these objectives were. And secondly, to locate them on the map. Which documents allow us to understand how your map functions in methodological terms?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I studied the documents of the sides involved in the conflict, and I singled out the documents which contained information on military targets, and on that basis I compiled a list of 24 documents which made reference to those targets. The list of documents is numbered from 1 to 25, and 24 documents because in the first list I made a mistake. One document was mentioned twice, so one list mentioned 24 documents, the other 25. Out of those 24 documents, in fact, 16 documents from the archives of the 1st Corps, they were provided to the Defence by the Prosecution and the Defence provided me with these documents, and those documents come from the archives of the SRK. On the basis of those 25 -- or rather, 24 documents, I compiled a list of military targets in Sarajevo according to the groups, as they were mentioned on the map, as they were indicated on the map. And furthermore, I marked the positions of those targets on the map, the ones that I managed to identify, since I have personal knowledge of Sarajevo, and this was also with the help of people who knew Sarajevo better than I did. So these documents consist of three parts: There's a list of documents, a list of targets, and then we have the targets marked on the map. So it's easy to check what sort of targets are in question if you take into consideration all these three groups of documents. That was the methodology I followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. With the assistance of the usher, I would like to hand out - but I think that these documents have already been provided to the registrar - the list of documents numbered D1915. I think I have a sufficient number of copies. If someone would like to take this document. Yes. That's the one, but we've already numbered it here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, could you confirm that this is the document you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was talking about this document. If you have a look at the number of the document, it's 15 and then 17. So the 16th one is one I repeated, so I removed it then, but so as not to disturb the series I am still left with the number 25, but in fact there are 24 documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. General, with regard to this document, there was a number of a document that was provided to you. Can you confirm this document that was shown to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the list that was already prepared. Madam Registrar, you marked it to the right of this list, but it must have been provided to you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. as one bundle. I don't know if you have it. If you don't have it, could you place it there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't want to waste too much time, but these documents were handed out. I know that we're working -- that we're going very fast. Can we show them to General Galic -- I apologise, to General Radinovic. That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, could you have a quick look at the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not quite sure which bundle of documents the Defence is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the Defence is referring to a bundle of documents which was presented to us in a greyish -- yes. I think that's the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This has now been marked as Defence 1915, this entire bundle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know. Because the list of documents is not numbered. All the documents listed seem to be -- to have been numbered. And they -- I find them next to the list itself. Does the list play any role, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, then it should be numbered as well, or would you like to whole bundle to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, because I'd like to witness to have a quick look at it and just say yes, that's it, so that I won't have any problems with regard to identification and so that I'm not told you've invented targets in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, have a look at the document. If you recognise it, you could say yes, that's the document I've seen and then we could move on to another subject. It's just a question of procedure.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise these documents, and I can confirm that this is the list, the one I've been provided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So that's the one that you used when writing your report and creating the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of the usher and Madam Registrar, could we have document 243, and we'll examine pages 0204 -- 02057541, page 4 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have this text in Serbian, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On which page? 131 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the booth asked --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The numbers that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I apologise. Document 243, D243. We'll have a look at the second page. The ERN number finished with numbers 541. The line starts with P/4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And general, after having had a glance at this document, could you tell us -- do you have the same page?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May it be put on the ELMO so that we have -- at least we know what the front page looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the second page on the screen, the one that finishes with the numbers 541.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you read the sentence that is underlined, that is to say, the one that starts at item 4.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's part of the document where the commander informs of his decision. "He decided that by relying on certain ground points, he should destroy the enemy."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have difficulties in finding 243, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Could perhaps the first -- Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I rise to object on the grounds that this is cumulative. Document 243 was a document Ms. Pilipovic showed this witness either late Thursday or early Friday and had the witness read out a portion of the same exact paragraph that Mr. Piletta-Zanin has now taken the witness to. You'll find it was about the, maybe, twelfth document that was shown to the witness. We've already -- we've already been over this area, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, could you confirm that you dealt with the same document, or is it something different?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's quite probable. It's quite probable. But my question was first of all: As we have seen many documents, I wanted to refresh the memory so that he could see what was at stake because he has seen hundreds of documents. If I can't do this, very well, I'll try to achieve the same effect by asking a lot of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Objection to say if I can't do that, if I can't question this. Would you please. You can do it. There's an objection. We are trying to find document 243 out of the big bundle. It would have certainly helped if you would have said this is a document Ms. Pilipovic went through already last Thursday, last Friday, so that in the heap of documents you have provided, part of them unnumbered, that we can find our way. You can do -- you are just responding to a -- to an objection. I have not given a decision, so there's no need whatsoever to complain about what you can do and what you cannot do. But we have to be in a position to follow the exercise. Otherwise, it will be useless -- the testimony will be useless if we are not in a position to follow closely what the expert witness tells us. Please proceed and refrain from similar comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'll have another comment at the end of the hearing. I'll need 30 seconds to expose something very clearly. And if possible, I will make the comment in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, document 243. My question is as follows -- and I would appreciate it if you could read this document out, if you could read the sentence that I mentioned to you out aloud.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "By relying on appropriate ground features, destroy the enemy at the forward end and spread panic among the Chetniks and civilians, then launch an attack," and then he mentions the direction Stupsko Brdo, the Nedzarici barracks, the theological faculty, Vojnicko Polje, Dobrinja V, Aleksa Santic primary school, the airport settlement, and he mentioned artillery preparation and the necessity of imposing great losses on the Chetniks, losses are to be imposed on the manpower and materiel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, with regard to what General Galic did, with regard to civilians, my question is as follows: Did you find any documents containing orders from General Galic which dealt with the issue of civilians? Did you come across any such documents?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, did you find only one document, or did you find several documents?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, what you were able to see -- according to what you were able to see yourself, what was the spirit and what were the contents of the orders issued by General Galic in these documents?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Galic issued orders that stated that civilians should not be deployed, or rather, that they should be positioned 5 kilometres behind the front in order to protect them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll stop you there in order to save time. With regard to the treatment of civilians, and in particular Muslim civilians, did General Galic issue any specific instructions; yes or no? What was the situation?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of instructions, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came across orders in which General Galic ordered his subordinates to behave in accordance with the Geneva Conventions in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. relation to the civilian population who were in the territory under the control of the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, the orders provided by General Galic that stated that the Geneva Conventions should be respected, were they repeated to the troops and what can you tell us with regard to the issue of trenches and combat?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as orders are concerned, General Galic requested in his documents that his officers and his men should respect the Geneva Conventions. There is almost -- there is not a single document -- there is barely a single document in which this isn't mentioned. So I didn't come across a document which would show that they did not respect these conventions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. General, I would now like to move on to other subjects, and perhaps we will return to this map if we have the time. But we're going to move on to more general issues. First of all, General, you were asked to dictate your observations for practical reasons. There were three or four observations. Did you have the time to do this? Because we haven't seen anything. If you have had the time to do so, perhaps during the break you could provide us with these documents so that we can familiarise ourselves with this and so that we can continue with your examination. And secondly, General, in your report you often use the term "civil war." I'd appreciate it if you could tell us why you use this term and what the practical distinctions are. What is the difference between a civil war and an ordinary war in reality on the ground?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I use the term "civil war" for the war in Sarajevo and in Bosnia-Herzegovina because it really had all the characteristics of a classical civil war. Why did I insist on using that term? Because the perception of military elements, the behaviour of the sides, the overview of the dynamics, the relation between the warring factions, the relation between the civilians and the soldiers, all these factors are quite different with regard to ordinary wars in which it's easy to distinguish the fronts. You know where the fronts are. You know who the warring factions are. The warring factions can be distinguished on the basis of the symbols that they bear. All the relations between civilians and soldiers are determined. It's easy to distinguish military and civilian objects. There is no confusion in this regard, and it's easy to assess whether principles of doctrine are being enforced in accordance with the rules of war or not. And in civil wars, this is not very reliable. It's very difficult. It's almost impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, could you briefly comment, if possible, on soldiers, on troops. I'm referring to infantry men involved in the reality of the conflict in an urban environment, someone who receives certain instructions but who also has to defend and defend himself. What is the influence of such a situation, of such a civil war on the specific -- on the particular attitude of a soldier in such an environment? Have you understood my question?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In such a conflict, the one that we are talking about, in militia military organisations where subordination is not very well defined and where the principle of participating on a voluntary basis in an army, where there is no war situation -- for example, where there are no clear symbol, where you can't distinguish uniforms and where people don't reside only in military buildings but also in civilian buildings. These are all elements which make it impossible for the organisation -- for the military organisation to be organised in a professional way, in a way that a well-organised army would do this. And the system of command suffers from -- fails more than in classical wars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, for technical reasons, I don't think we'll have the time to go into your observations, during the break to familiarise ourselves with your observations. This is why I'm asking you about it now. You wanted to comment on your text. It wasn't a purely technical comment. It didn't concern errors, but it had to do with the substance. And I think that I know that it has to do with the matter of distinctions, with making distinctions. What can you tell us about this in relation to your report? What can you tell us about this distinction?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. The question is not clear. If Mr. Piletta-Zanin is referring to distinction as a legal term, that's not a proper question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm in a stalemate situation because we don't have the amendments that you wanted to have written. I don't think we'll have them when we carry on with this testimony. I think that I know what the witness would like to say. If you would allow me to be leading here, I'll be very clear. But otherwise, for technical reasons, I'll not be able to put this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll consider to -- whether we'd allow you to do this during the break. Could you give us a brief indication on to what subject you'd like to add something. Just mention the subject, not your changes you'd like to make. But on what subject would you like to change your report or adapt your report or ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That has to do with distinguishing civilians from soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. After the break you can put some questions. And it's -- the witness now identified himself what was the area on which he would like to make any changes to his report. Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom so that Mr. Piletta-Zanin has the 30 seconds he asked for to give a -- to submit something. You said you would like to do that in open court.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, at the end of the hearing, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any specific reason why -- well, this is the end of the first part. But is there any reason why not to do it at this very moment, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it will be at the end of the hearing or not. If it's not possible, it doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll allow you to do that. But the only thing I'm adding to it is that if you wait until then, of course it can have no -- we cannot draw any consequences of what you tell us during the examination of this witness. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could get an indication of approximately how much time remains for direct examination, that would be very helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I asked the new -- I'll give you an indication after the break. We'll adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The time spent until now on examination-in-chief is approximately four hours, a little bit over four hours. The Chamber has indicated before that it would certainly -- if extra time would be granted, it would not be more than one hour, up to five hours. Therefore, the examination-in-chief should end by approximately 12.00. That would bring you to five hours. And then the Prosecution would have five hours as well. You may proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you were about to indicate, with respect to the modifications to your report, something about what you wrote. In your report, as we can read it in English, we see that at a certain point you practically established the principle of identity of fighters and of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. civilians in Sarajevo. Could you please clarify your position and state exactly what you understand by this.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this part of my report, I was talking about the identity of civilians and soldiers respectively. I thought that it was a military matter, a military problem, and it is simply understood that this category of identities of civilians and soldiers refers exclusively to the identity of males, able-bodied men. We must certainly rule out children, the elderly, and the greatest part of women because we know from documents that there were also women in the BH army. But certainly the greatest percentage of women is excluded from this category. I simply overlooked this. I didn't even think it is an error because we know from the context that it is able-bodied men who are meant by this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Precisely. With respect to able-bodied men, are there in the history of the Sarajevo war certain periods of time in which it was more difficult for factual reasons, for reasons related to the situation, and other periods where this distinction was more difficult to make? I'm talking about able-bodied men of military age. What can you tell us about this?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the war, it was very difficult to distinguish between civilians and soldiers. But in the dynamics of war, there were periods when this was easier and periods when it was more difficult. It was the most difficult at the beginning of the war until mid-1993, and from then on it was a little easier but it was never easy to make a clear distinction, to be absolutely certain in the difference between civilians and soldiers. But in this period when it was the most difficult, this has to do with notorious facts that are characteristic for this war, which means that the armies on both sides, and especially the BH army, did not have uniforms, so as far as clothing is concerned, there was absolutely no distinction. General Siber, who was deputy general of the BH army -- deputy commander of the BH army, wrote in his book that they received their first uniforms only in the end of November, but even when they got them one could expect - and we could see that also on video footage, on the tapes that I have seen - that both soldiers and civilians wore parts of uniform, plus soldiers wore some civilian clothes as well. You could also see from my own contributions and from documents which I've come across that in the command system of the BH army, the commanders did not refrain at all from using civilian facilities for placing military equipment. In the BH army but also in the Sarajevo Romanija Corps and in the VRS it was the case that the army lived and operated in precisely the same environment as the civilians. When they were not waging war, they rested in both military and civilian facilities. So the military structure was not clearly separated from civilian facilities, and it was simply impossible to make the distinction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like us to place ourselves in the shoes of a soldier on either side who is defending his territory. In your personal experience of a high-ranking military man, what could be the position of such a soldier when he sees at a small distance from him somebody he cannot immediately identify but who appears to be of male sex in what we call the combat zone, meaning his immediate zone of responsibility or close to him?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood your question correctly, it is simply expected that all the troops located in the so-called tactical depth - and that means an area where the battalions of the 1st front line are deployed, that is, their combat disposition - it is simply expected that this area is free of civilians. This is a doctrinary principle. In the city it is simply impossible. And I have heard the testimony of some military leaders of the 1st Corps. I think it was the commander of the Dobrinja Brigade who said that they could not separate civilians from soldiers. I know it was difficult, but that makes the risk so much higher. So the commander does not expect to find civilians within the tactical depth. It is a doctrinary obligation and everyone who fails to observe that take upon themselves the risk for possible civilian losses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are talking about the commander of the Dobrinja Brigade. Do you remember his name?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Ismet Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk to him personally?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's the commander of the 5th Dobrinja Brigade of the 1st BH army Corps. I would have liked to talk to him, but I'm afraid that at the time when I was making my report and when I was in Sarajevo, I don't think he would be happy to talk to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have the impression that this commander of the 5th Brigade, was it a question of principle or was it something that he lived himself, this difficulty of distinguishing who is who?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand your question, or maybe it was a question of translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking: This answer provided by this military man, did it regard a military principle or was it something that he had to live through, his personal experience?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that he replied to me. He replied to a question asked him in the courtroom, why he didn't distinguish soldiers from civilians. I think he was sincere in saying that. In that type of war it was absolutely impossible to make the distinction between soldiers and civilians. But I think that the commanders were not responsible enough. They could have done more for the protection of civilians, evacuating them, at least temporarily from the area of combat activities. But I admit it was impossible to carry out to the full.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more question to finish with this topic: Until which distance -- up to which distance the human eye can identify details of a human silhouette?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, beyond the scope of this witness's expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us check, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, in the military technique, are there scientific data that are taught to officers, particularly regarding what a human eye can distinguish, depending on distance?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a certain part of training is called the training of observers. Observers on the front line using not only instruments but also the naked eye collect data.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally, do you have any knowledge of this scientific data as to what the naked eye can see and cannot see at a certain distance?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to pass to another question. You said in your -- one of your answers on Friday that General Galic had to observe his military hierarchy and specifically his general staff concerning specifically a protest by the other party, by the other side, or the UNPROFOR. I would now like to ask you to specify what you meant by that. Did this pose difficulties? What did you mean?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand you quite well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll rephrase. Yesterday you told us from what you saw that the general conveyed protests when they were made to the general staff. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Now I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this factor, the existence of this hierarchical scheme, what did it represent to General Galic? Was it an obstacle or what? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sarajevo, General Galic was between several fires, if we can put it that way metaphorically. Above him he had the general staff of the VRS as his superior command. He had his subordinates in the chain of command, to whom he had to convey certain orders. But he also had above him the civilian part of the superior command, as a parallel command of sorts. At the same time, there was this whole conglomerate of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. international organisations, including the UNPROFOR, who imposed demands on him. That's the civilian part of the high command, the military part of the high command, and the UNPROFOR. So he was receiving a lot of requests, and the relationship with the UNPROFOR was regulated by the general staff. Therefore, Galic had obligations without having the right to make decisions. That's why he was between two fires and he was always exposed to reproaches and had the obligation to comply with demands. As far as the UNPROFOR is concerned, he responded to every reproach made to him, either by initiating an investigation with regard to the facts, or by demanding certain action from his subordinates. But most of his responses were directed at the superior command that was above him and which restricted his communication with the UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very briefly, in two words: This confusion and this multitude of components, the civil part of the command, the military part of the command, and the international organisations, did it render General Galic's task even more difficult? What was the general conclusion you made?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was certainly one of the major impeding factors in Galic's command system.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, now, could you please answer the following question: How many documents did you have to examine in order to write your report over these two years? I don't want you to be very precise. Just give me an order of value. More than 200? More than 500? More than 1.000, or just in the hundreds?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I didn't count them, but if I remember the volume of binders that I had to deal with, I think it was over 5.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, in all these documents that you have seen - and I'm not talking obviously about the indictment - did you see a single document dated in the period from September 1992 to August 1994 addressed to General Galic that had to do with terrorist acts or something similar to that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you look at the transcript, I see -- I see that what I understood to be "actes de terreur," has been translated by "terrorist acts". But I think you said "acts of terror"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It is difficult for me to follow everything and to read. We are talking indeed about acts of terror. I'll rephrase the question because the English transcript is not quite what I would like it to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... The question put to you, General, was that -- did you understand that to be asked about whether there was any mentioning of acts of terror or acts of terrorists? How did you understand the question that you just answered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood the question to deal with acts of terror, not terrorist acts, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another question, a major question of principle, General: In the documents that you were able to study, were you able to determine at which level in the BH army were the mortars, small and large calibres, deployed; brigade, corps, or other level?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, relevance, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this was intended to solicit a response from the witness, especially in view of certain techniques related to the use of these weapons. I think we have already heard about it. It is doubtlessly important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the units had the ammunition that had this sort of weapon. Companies had 60-millimetre mortars; battalion firing groups had ammo for 82-millimetre mortars, and brigades had ammo for 120-millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question had to do with the BH army, that is, the Army of the Presidency, as we term it here. I don't know if you understood.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood. That is the principle that applied to both armies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. My question didn't have to do with who had the ammunition but who literally -- for the B/C/S booth, not the ammunition but the weapons. Who had the power to order fire from these mortars? Who commanded the use of mortars? Was it at the level of battalion, the corps, or what level?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Weapons are within the organisational military establishment of units. Every commander has the right to order activity from his unit unless forbidden by his superior. I didn't see in any documents that the BH army prohibited the use of their weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. We are now going to pass to questions of principles. On page 9 of your report, in the English version -- sorry, page 49 of your report in the English version, you mentioned a certain number of strategic and military objectives.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you think I will need the report in front of me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you have it, yes, please, take it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the Court copy could be at the disposal of the expert witness. Do we have the report, Madam Registrar? Otherwise, the -- Then if you put it on the ELMO and put it in front of you so we can see whether we have the same page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are talking about item 102. And I can gladly provide my own copy with things underlined in it. But I can provide it, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... You have no copy, General? You have no copy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's in my bag. I don't want to take it without your approval.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
